responses.strategic_rationale: Establishing a residential NREM parasomnia unit in Bonn requires balancing ecological validity with safety, regulatory compliance, and rigorous data quality. The levers focus on data governance, staffing resilience, triage architecture, recruitment optimization, environmental design, and disciplined budgeting to navigate tensions between speed, cost, scope, and reliability. This set aims to create an iterative, scalable research program that yields scientifically valid phenotyping and methods validation, while avoiding premature deployment of autonomous diagnostic claims.

levers.name: Sensing architecture and data governance
levers.consequences: Tiered sensing architecture reduces privacy risk and data handling burden on routine nights, enabling safer broader sharing and easier integration into a data warehouse. It also introduces escalation points that require coordination and may delay capturing infrequent events if responders are unavailable, creating potential data gaps during peak periods. Edge-case policy adjustments and staff training may be required.
options: Implement a tiered sensing protocol prioritizing dry-electrode EEG and mattress sensors for baseline nights, enabling full PSG only on escalation nights after predefined triggers.
Institute strict de-identification and access controls across datasets before external collaboration, anchored by a data steward and formal audit trails.
Establish formal data use agreements and partner registries to ensure traceable, compliant data sharing while maintaining core privacy protections.
levers.review_lever: Tiered sensing offers privacy protection and data richness, but escalation triggers risk gaps if responders cannot reach events in time, potentially delaying Aim 1 milestones.

levers.name: Staffing model and shift design for 8 active suites
levers.consequences: Ensures safety coverage across all 8 active suites and supports timely event response and annotation throughput. However, external standby staff increases variable costs and demands additional onboarding and training alignment with core team workflows.
options: Institute rotating night shifts with cross-trained technicians to ensure safety response and consistent annotation throughput across all active suites.
Adopt structured overlapping shifts with an on-call escalation mechanism to balance safety requirements with predictable labor costs.
Contract external standby staff for peak-risk periods, preserving core team stability while managing variability in event response.
levers.review_lever: Flexible staffing enhances safety coverage across eight suites, yet reliance on external supplemental staff can erode consistency and raise cost volatility if onboarding lags.

levers.name: Event-triage tool development and validation
levers.consequences: Advancing triage capabilities will reduce manual review workload and accelerate phenotyping, but early accuracy depends on data quality and inter-rater consistency, which can delay milestones. Effective validation is essential to maintain confidence in phenotyping results.
options: Develop a data-driven event-triage model trained on adjudicated episodes, incorporating a robust human-in-the-loop validation workflow.
Adopt a transparent rule-based triage framework with pre-defined criteria to prioritize clinician review and preserve interpretability.
Limit automated triage to retrospective analysis during the initial phase, ensuring patient safety through manual scoring during real-time monitoring.
levers.review_lever: Developing a triage model reduces manual scoring, but early accuracy hinges on data quality and scorer consistency, risking slower progress toward the Aim 2 phenotyping milestone.

levers.name: Recruitment pathways and retention safeguards
levers.consequences: Improved recruitment trajectory accelerates enrollment toward target; however, too lenient criteria may increase heterogeneity and affect interpretability of longitudinal patterns. Maintaining strict pre-admission screening can safeguard safety but may slow initial enrollment.
options: Coordinate recruitment through University Hospital Bonn, regional neurologists, and professional networks, implementing structured pre-admission screening and collateral history to reduce dropouts.
Provide enhanced participant engagement through clear milestones, regular feedback, and transparent expectations to improve retention during extended stays.
Implement adaptive inclusion criteria reviews at predefined milestones to maintain enrollment targets without compromising safety.
levers.review_lever: Recruitment optimization accelerates enrollment, but overly broad criteria may increase heterogeneity and complicate interpretation of longitudinal patterns.

levers.name: Environmental design and safety balance
levers.consequences: Preserves naturalistic behavior supports data fidelity and participant comfort, yet safety features may introduce perceptible cues that change sleep behavior, requiring careful monitoring and gradual adjustments during the pilot phase.
options: Maintain a home-like interior with discreet safety upgrades and rapid access points to ensure safety without compromising naturalistic behavior.
Introduce visible safety control points and secure observation spaces that reassure staff while preserving a domestic ambience.
Develop flexible room configurations that can adapt to increased event density while maintaining participant comfort.
levers.review_lever: Environmental design preserves comfort and data fidelity, yet safety features may introduce perceptible cues that change sleep behavior, requiring careful monitoring and gradual adjustments during the pilot phase.

levers.name: Budget governance and milestone gating
levers.consequences: Linking spending to progress drives accountability but rigid gates may delay critical hires or equipment procurement if milestones slip, risking data quality or recruitment pace.
options: Institute milestone-based expenditures with quarterly reviews that reallocate funds toward data quality improvements and recruitment acceleration.
Prioritize core operations in year one with a contingency reserve for equipment upgrades and regulatory approvals to prevent disruption.
Engage external audits and scenario planning to detect potential overruns early and preserve sustainability across all three years.
levers.review_lever: Budget governance aligns spending with progress, but rigid gates may delay critical hires or equipment procurement if milestones slip, risking data quality or recruitment pace.

responses.strategic_rationale: The Bonn residential parasomnia unit faces tensions among data fidelity, participant experience in a domestic-like setting, and long-run funding for a multi-year program. The levers center on sequencing enrollment to align with data quality and safety validation, instituting robust privacy-preserving data governance, enabling scalable facility design that preserves ambience while accommodating growth, blending automated and clinician-augmented event triage to manage workload, aligning participant incentives with sustainable budgets, building staffing resilience without impeding training, and leveraging external collaborations to sustain momentum and secure future grants. Together these levers address safety, data quality, staffing risk, and long-term viability of a methods-focused research platform.

levers.name: Phased intake cadence aligned to data quality milestones
levers.consequences: Staged participant intake aligns with safety reviews and data pipeline validation, reducing bottlenecks in annotation throughput during the pilot phase. Downstream, full capacity deployment is contingent on achieving data quality milestones, which may delay rapid scaling to 12 suites and extend the time to reach enrollment targets.
options: Implement a phased intake cadence that ramps stays from 8 active suites to full capacity only after initial data-quality milestones are met.
Adopt rolling enrollment with fixed weekly intake windows to maintain consistent staffing and annotation throughput regardless of individual event yield.
Prioritize high-risk participants into early cohorts with enhanced monitoring to validate safety protocols before expanding to the broader pool.
levers.review_lever: Rolling intake aligned to data milestones stabilizes early data collection, but may slow scaling if milestones slip and occupancy lags behind planned expansion.

levers.name: Cross-domain data access governance with privacy-preserving pipelines
levers.consequences: This approach creates formal data-use boundaries and audit trails, enabling de-identified sharing with collaborators while maintaining privacy controls. The trade-off is increased governance overhead and potential delays in data availability for external validation until approvals are updated.
options: Implement de-identified data export with controlled tokens and revocation, enabling selective external collaboration without compromising patient privacy.
Establish a formal data-use agreement template and review cadence to synchronize access rights with evolving project milestones.
Institute a privacy-preserving federated analysis pilot that avoids raw data transfers while enabling multi-site validation.
levers.review_lever: Cross-domain governance enables compliant collaboration, but adds review cycles that can delay data sharing and slow external validation until agreements and templates are fully established.

levers.name: Facility modularity and safety-enabled room reconfiguration
levers.consequences: Rooms can be reconfigured for enhanced safety or expanded capacity; downstream, expansion to 12 suites can be achieved with minimal renovation disruption, but requires upfront modular equipment and logistics coordination. This approach reduces long-run renovation risk but introduces upfront procurement complexity.
options: Install modular partition systems and adjustable safety features to reconfigure spaces quickly for different study phases.
Adopt a phased renovation blueprint that pre-install scalable infrastructure and flexible utilities to support future expansion.
Create a safety-first room design library mapping risk profiles to configurable layout templates and staffing plans.
levers.review_lever: Modularity supports rapid reconfiguration and safety upgrades, yet introduces upfront procurement complexity and coordination needs that may extend initial facility setup and disrupt ongoing data collection.

levers.name: Hybrid event-triage workflow with clinician-augmented scoring
levers.consequences: By combining algorithmic triage with clinician review at key milestones, this lever improves accuracy of event classification while maintaining review throughput. However, it increases scheduling needs for clinicians and may slow immediate output during peak periods.
options: Implement clinician-augmented triage that flags high-fidelity events for rapid review while auto-classifying routine patterns efficiently.
Adopt adaptive scoring thresholds based on patient cohort to balance sensitivity and false positives during night transitions.
Adopt a lightweight, checklist-driven annotation protocol to standardize manual review while minimizing cognitive load on staff.
levers.review_lever: Hybrid event-triage with clinician input improves accuracy but increases scheduling demands for clinicians, potentially slowing throughput during peak stay weeks.

levers.name: Participant incentive and retention design across stay durations
levers.consequences: Enhanced compensation and amenities improves adherence, reduces dropout risk, and increases data yield. Downstream, budget pressure rises and may constrain other program areas if funding does not keep pace.
options: Structure milestone-based participant engagement with escalating compensation aligned to completion of enhanced-night PSG nights milestones.
Offer flexible scheduling and respite accommodations to minimize fatigue and promote long-stay participation across extended stays.
Implement partner-assisted collateral history collection with caregiver support to boost enrollment quality and retention rates.
levers.review_lever: Enhanced incentives improve retention and data yield, but require careful budgeting and monitoring to avoid creating inequities or unsustainable burn rates.

levers.name: Staffing model resilience and cross-training for night shifts
levers.consequences: Cross-training staff reduces risk of coverage gaps and ensures safety during nights, boosting throughput. Downstream, it increases training overhead and role clarity challenges during initial ramp-up.
options: Establish cross-trained technician teams capable of monitoring multiple suites and performing preliminary scoring on-site during night shifts.
Institute a reserve on-call roster to cover unexpected absences without compromising safety or response time.
Rotate staff across night shifts and day shifts to balance fatigue, coverage, and experience levels.
levers.review_lever: Resilient staffing reduces single-point failures and ensures safety coverage, yet cross-training raises upfront training time and role clarity challenges during initial ramp-up.

levers.name: External collaboration and phased publication milestones
levers.consequences: Engaging external collaborators and publishing incrementally can validate methods and unlock future funding, while potentially slowing internal decision cycles due to review processes.
options: Launch a formal collaboration incubator with selective academia and pharma partners to align on validation milestones.
Publish early-methods papers and data descriptors to demonstrate transparency and attract grant support from diverse funders.
Schedule quarterly progress reviews with the external advisory board to synchronize research aims with funding opportunities.
levers.review_lever: External collaboration and phased publications build credibility and funding prospects, but competing priorities and review cycles may slow internal decision-making and milestone execution.

levers.name: Data governance and privacy preservation plan enforcement

options: Develop a formal de-identification workflow for all sensor streams and restrict access to bedroom video to authorized personnel only.

levers.name: Recruitment pre-screen and consent pipeline optimization

options: Centralize structured pre-admission pathway with standardized collateral history collection to improve enrollment efficiency and ensure eligibility consistency across sites.

levers.name: Shift design and cross-training for safe 24/7 coverage

system_prompt:
You are an expert strategic analyst. Generate solution space parameters following these directives:

1. **Output Requirements**
   - You must generate 5 to 7 levers per response.
   - Each lever's `options` field must contain exactly 3 qualitative strategic choices as plain strings.

2. **Lever Quality Standards**
   - Consequences: describe the direct effect of pulling this lever, then at least one downstream implication or trade-off. Use numbers only when the project context provides them directly — do not calculate, derive, or estimate figures. Target length: 2–3 sentences.
   - Options MUST:
     • Represent genuinely distinct strategic pathways (not just labels)
     • Include at least one unconventional or non-obvious approach
     • NO prefixes (e.g., "Option A:", "Choice 1:")

3. **Strategic Framing**
   - Name each lever using language drawn directly from the project's own domain — avoid formulaic patterns or repeated prefixes
   - Frame options as complete strategic approaches
   - Ensure levers challenge core project assumptions

4. **Validation Protocols**
   - For `review_lever`:
     A one-sentence critical review. Examples:
     - "Switching from seasonal contract labor to year-round employees stabilizes harvest quality, but the idle-wage burden during the 5-month off-season adds a fixed cost that erases the per-unit savings unless utilization reaches year-round levels."
     - "Each additional clinical site requires its own IRB approval, site-initiation visit, and staff credentialing — a sequential overhead that compounds rather than parallelizes, so doubling site count does not halve enrollment time."
     - "Pooling catastrophe risk across three coastal regions reduces expected annual loss on paper, but a single regional hurricane season can correlate all three simultaneously, turning the diversification assumption into a concentration risk at the worst possible moment."
     Do not use square brackets or placeholder text.

5. **Prohibitions**
   - NO prefixes/labels in options (e.g., "Option A:", "Choice 1:")
   - NO generic option labels (e.g., "Optimize X", "Tolerate Y")
   - NO placeholder consequences or bracket-wrapped templates
   - NO calculated, derived, or estimated figures — use only numbers that appear verbatim in the project context
   - NO marketing language (e.g., "game-changing", "cutting-edge", "revolutionary")

6. **Length Limits**
   - Keep each `review_lever` to one sentence (20–40 words).
   - Each option should be a concrete, actionable approach (at least 15 words with an action verb) — not a short label or vague aspiration
   - Maintain parallel grammatical structure across options
   - Ensure options are self-contained descriptions

Plan:
Establish a 3-year residential longitudinal research unit in Bonn, Germany, for the study of adult NREM parasomnias — sleepwalking, confusional arousals, and sleep terrors — with a secondary exploratory arm for REM sleep behavior disorder under a separate protocol with dedicated neurologic screening, reflecting RBD's distinct clinical trajectory per current AASM guidance. The facility is affiliated with University Hospital Bonn's Department of Epileptology, leveraging its existing long-term video-EEG monitoring culture, and addresses a specific methodological gap: traditional single-night polysomnography rarely captures infrequent parasomnia events, while outpatient actigraphy lacks physiological resolution. The unit houses 8 active sleep suites at launch in a converted residential property in a quiet Bonn neighborhood, renovated for safety (padded corridor edges, restricted-opening windows, silent exterior door alarms, fire safety, acoustic treatment, network cabling, accessibility modifications) while preserving a domestic feel — if the environment is too clinical, naturalistic behavior is suppressed. Physical capacity exists for 12 suites, but expansion is deferred until the pilot proves acceptable data quality, manageable false alarm rates, safe staffing ratios, and usable annotation throughput. Sensing uses a tiered acquisition model: nightly low-burden monitoring via dry-electrode EEG headbands, contact-free mattress sensors, unobtrusively mounted infrared cameras, ambient microphones, and environmental sensors; scheduled enhanced nights with fuller PSG montage including standard scalp EEG, EOG, chin EMG, and leg EMG on the first night, one mid-stay night, and the final night per participant; and escalation nights deploying full PSG after technician-flagged events to capture recurrence at clinical-grade resolution. All streams are time-synchronized and stored in EEG-BIDS-compatible format on a local NAS with nightly encrypted backup to university storage, annotated in real time by the night technician and later scored by two independent raters using AASM criteria with inter-rater reliability reported. Public data sharing is limited to de-identified physiological and sensor data under data use agreements — bedroom video carries severe privacy constraints and is not deposited in public repositories. The scientific program has three explicit aims: Aim 1, establish and operationally validate the residential capture model as safe, ethics-approved, and sustainable; Aim 2, characterize within-person and between-person parasomnia patterns longitudinally, including episode frequency, morphology, triggers, and temporal clustering; Aim 3, develop and benchmark semi-automated event-triage tools that rank probable parasomnia episodes and reduce manual review burden, evaluated against dual human scorer agreement rather than promising autonomous diagnosis.

Participant recruitment targets adults aged 18–65 with NREM parasomnia confirmed through a structured pre-admission pathway: specialist clinical interview, collateral history from bed partner or household member where available, prior or screening polysomnography, and a structured exclusion checklist adjudicated by the PI. Explicit exclusions are nocturnal epilepsy or suspected epilepsy mimics, untreated obstructive sleep apnea, active major substance use disorder, severe psychiatric instability, and wandering or injury risk beyond facility capability. Recruitment channels are the University Hospital Bonn sleep clinic, regional neurologist referrals, and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Schlafforschung und Schlafmedizin network, with per-night compensation of €80 plus meals. A matched control group provides baseline nocturnal movement, arousal patterns, and false-positive sensor activity under identical residential monitoring conditions, enabling benchmarking of the event-triage tools against normal nocturnal behavior. Event-yield planning assumes that based on the inclusion criterion of at least 2 self-reported episodes per month, approximately 70–80% of admitted participants will produce at least one captured and adjudicated event during a 2–8 week stay; stays may be extended up to 2 additional weeks for participants with zero captured events after the initial period, capped at 10 weeks total, with a protocol ceiling of 20% unproductive admissions before triggering a recruitment-criteria review. The core team is 9 people: a PI who is a board-certified sleep medicine physician, 2 postdoctoral researchers in sleep neurophysiology and computational neuroscience respectively, 3 research technicians rotating night shifts to ensure safe coverage of 8 active suites with adequate margin for event response and annotation, a clinical psychologist specializing in sleep disorders, a data engineer managing the sensor pipeline, and a study coordinator handling recruitment, consent, scheduling, and ethics compliance.

Budget is €3.8 million over 3 years, gated: €1.8M year one covering property lease and renovation at approximately €750K, equipment at approximately €450K, staff hiring accounting for German social insurance contributions and actual overnight coverage, ethics approval, and a pilot cohort of 15–20 participants; €1.2M year two covering full operations with 30–35 participants, the enhanced-night PSG program, first publications, and event-triage algorithm development; €800K year three conditional on demonstrable progress by month 24. Personnel costs are approximately €2M over three years and remaining funds cover participant compensation, independent scoring time, data storage and retention, regulatory and legal work, and contingency. Funding sources are DFG research grant and University of Bonn internal research funding as the primary pillars, with a pharmaceutical industry partnership as optional upside rather than a feasibility requirement — if secured, the academic team retains full publication rights with the pharma partner receiving a 30-day pre-publication comment window only. Success criteria at 36 months: safe residential monitoring operations sustained for at least 24 months, enrollment of 50–70 NREM parasomnia participants plus matched controls, capture of a prespecified minimum number of independently adjudicated parasomnia events sufficient for Aim 2 phenotyping analysis, 2–3 peer-reviewed publications in sleep medicine journals covering methods validation and longitudinal characterization, a benchmarked semi-automated event-triage model with reported sensitivity, specificity, and agreement against dual human scoring, de-identified physiological dataset deposited in a recognized repository, and a submitted phase-two grant proposal for expansion and intervention studies. Failure triggers: if by month 18 the facility has enrolled fewer than 25 participants or captured fewer than 40 adjudicated events, the program undergoes external review. Governance is a 3-member external scientific advisory board reviewing progress every 6 months, with the PI holding operational authority and budget reallocations above €50K requiring board approval. Banned words: AI, blockchain, app, VR, AR, gamification, wearable startup, consumer product, DAO, NFT, metaverse, smart home, autonomous diagnosis, digital therapeutic, SaaS, marketplace, validated (in the context of claiming a mature deployable system). Pick a realistic scenario — this is an early-stage clinical research facility producing methods validation and phenotyping work, not a finished diagnostic platform.
